name: Fox
overview: The Bible uses the image of the fox to illustrate both literal and figurative truths. Samson's capture of foxes to burn the Philistines' fields (Judges 15:4) highlights their role in destruction, while Nehemiah 4:3 shows how even a fox can undermine a stone wall, symbolizing vulnerability. Figuratively, prophets who lead Israel astray are likened to foxes in the desert (Ezekiel 13:4), representing craftiness and unfaithfulness. Jesus contrasts the foxes' secure homes with His own homelessness (Matthew 8:20; Luke 9:58), underscoring His earthly sacrifice and the contempt faced by His mission.
